summary: Roadmap organized around evidence rather than historical milestone labels: repository code and detailed specs do not count as released behavior until the release bar is met. Current foundation inventories the canonical model and escrow, live format adapters, CLI and Studio import/edit/validation/conversion/export, local storage and editors, sealed script analysis and opt-in benches, and source-preview Kit with providers, staged changes, sessions, content capabilities, and indexed docs retrieval; Kit is run with bun run kit and is absent from current release binaries. Near-term release work covers quiet artifact-level verification, exact public contracts, authenticated and signed release artifacts, and making Kit distributable with complete content lifecycles and real-terminal tests. Product work after the release foundation sequences Script Doctor, Table Read, Test Stage and productions, and Archives and World Forge while preserving canonical storage, staged edits, sealed scripts, citations, and deterministic foundations. Release bars require real public behavior, boundary and regression tests, live installed-flow proof, current reference documentation, and smoke-tested release artifacts before any milestone is called complete.

sections.title: Current foundation
sections.summary: The implemented foundation includes a canonical content model with escrowed source data, live format detection and adapters represented by FORMAT-SUPPORT, and import, validation, conversion, and export through both CLI and Studio. Studio provides local storage and the editors documented in the UI reference. Lua and regex payloads remain sealed during normal work and are analyzed or run only in user-invoked benches. Source-preview Kit already includes provider setup, staged mutations, sessions, content capabilities, and indexed documentation retrieval. Exact behavior belongs to the support matrix and CLI/UI references. Kit currently starts from source with bun run kit and is not included in GitHub release binaries.

sections.title: Near-term release work
sections.summary: Near-term work is release engineering rather than a claim that repository features are already product-complete. Make verification complete and quiet by removing OpenTUI warning noise and exercising real Node and packaged artifacts. Make public contracts exact by synchronizing documentation and proving the round-trip fidelity each adapter claims. Make releases reproducible by embedding the sidecar, running the full wall, auditing dependencies, pinning build inputs, authenticating existing checksums, and adding signatures. Finish Kit as a distributable product by packaging it, completing native content lifecycles, retaining staged approval and validation, and testing providers, recovery, docs retrieval, and editing in supported terminals.

children.title: Make verification complete and quiet
children.summary: Verification already discovers tests across src and scripts and lints both React surfaces. Remaining work removes noisy React act warnings from the OpenTUI harness so genuine regressions stand out, then makes Node and packaged-binary smoke checks execute the actual artifacts users receive. The goal is to close the gap between source-tree confidence and release confidence without listing already-shipped gates as future work.

children.title: Make public contracts exact
children.summary: Architecture, security, CLI, and UI references must move with implementation. Canonical boundary validation and semantic-summary freshness are current foundation rather than future roadmap items. Remaining contract work centers on proving same-format semantic round trips at the fidelity tier each adapter advertises instead of relying on generic tests or broad claims.

children.title: Make releases reproducible
children.summary: Supported release artifacts must contain the remote-access sidecar instead of depending on a checkout. Tagging follows the complete verification wall and a transitive production-dependency audit. Build actions and tools are pinned exactly to prevent moving inputs. Releases already publish checksums; remaining work must authenticate those checksum records and add signatures, giving users verifiable identity and making a release repeatable rather than merely buildable on one maintainer's machine.

children.title: Finish Kit as a distributable product
children.summary: Kit must move from bun run kit in a source checkout to a supported packaged entry point. Native create and edit flows must cover every supported content kind. Mutations must retain composed previews, explicit user approval, revision checks, and deterministic validation. Provider setup and recovery, documentation retrieval, and complete content lifecycles need live testing in real terminals across supported operating systems before distribution is claimed complete.

sections.title: Product work after the release foundation
sections.summary: Product expansion follows the release foundation and reuses existing contracts instead of creating parallel systems. Script Doctor starts with deterministic field-cited analysis and keeps model treatments staged. Table Read turns interviews into ordinary canonical edits through the same validation, storage, and history paths as direct editing. Test Stage and productions extend assembly, replay, history, and multi-piece workspaces while leaving imported scripts sealed outside existing benches. Archives and World Forge derive characters and continuity knowledge from large conversation collections, with evidence attached to every derived claim. Their detailed designs live under feature and engine specs, but those specs are not shipping evidence.

children.title: Script Doctor
children.summary: Script Doctor begins with deterministic content analysis so useful findings do not require a provider. Every finding identifies the affected canonical field. Optional model assistance may propose treatment plans, but edits remain staged for review rather than silently applied. The contracts under specs/features govern the future implementation and must be reconciled with the same validation and mutation paths used elsewhere.

children.title: Table Read
children.summary: Table Read is an interview-led authoring experience whose output is not a special conversational document. Answers become ordinary canonical edits, then use the same local storage, validation, and history mechanisms as direct Workbench changes. That shared path prevents interview-created characters and lore from drifting into a second content model or bypassing established mutation safeguards.

children.title: Test Stage and productions
children.summary: Test Stage and productions extend prompt assembly, replay, content history, and multi-piece workspace behavior. They must remain extensions of the canonical model rather than introducing production-only entity shapes. Imported Lua, macros, regex, and other executable-looking payloads stay sealed as content throughout those workflows, with execution permitted only through the already isolated, explicitly invoked Lua and regex test benches.

children.title: Archives and World Forge
children.summary: Archives and World Forge target evidence-backed extraction from large conversation histories and continuity work across multiple pieces. Summaries, character facts, lore, and contradiction findings derived from archives must retain citations to the source material that supports them. The citation requirement is part of the product contract, preventing generated continuity claims from becoming unattributed canonical facts.

sections.title: Release bars
sections.summary: A milestone is complete only when behavior exists outside fixtures, boundary and regression coverage plus adjacent tests pass, user-facing flows work live in a real installation, reference pages describe the implementation without substituting future tense, and the actual release artifact passes smoke testing. Repository code, passing unit tests, or a detailed specification is insufficient alone. Historical jewel names and dates remain available through Git history for archaeology, but this roadmap deliberately does not use them as evidence of current status.
